pattern_title: CO inpatient spend rose across product, PA, and facility mix
pattern_description: CO shows the largest operational pressure, but it is not coming from one simple source. PPO CHILDRENS admissions requiring PA increased, EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL cases without PA also increased, and PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL cases showed added spend even as volume fell because paid per admit rose. The business story is a combined product, PA, and facility mix issue rather than a single utilization spike.

claims.summary: CO PPO CHILDRENS with PA added about $1.5M, with admissions up 7 and paid per admit up about $20.7K. CO EPO ACUTE HOSPITAL without PA added about $1.3M, with admissions up 5 and paid per admit up about $21.0K. CO PPO ACUTE HOSPITAL with PA added about $0.6M even as admissions fell 16, pointing to unit-cost pressure rather than volume growth.

The policy does not name or price this postpartum/postabortion DRG category; it governs inpatient readmission reimbursement. For New York Medicaid, an unplanned readmission within 14 days for the same or closely related condition or procedure is not separately reimbursed when it occurs to the same or a different hospital within the same hospital system. Obstetrical deliveries are excluded, so postpartum/postabortion cases are implicated only if they are not treated as delivery admissions.

individual_policies.evidence: The policy does not cite the requested maternity DRG category or postpartum preeclampsia specifically. For New York inpatient claims paid under DRG methodology, unplanned readmissions within 14 days to the same or a different hospital in the same hospital system for the same, similar, or related condition or procedure are not separately reimbursed unless an exclusion applies. Obstetrical deliveries are generally excluded, but postpartum or postabortion readmissions are not separately listed as excluded in the New York rule.
